paper_id: Li et al. - 2013 - Sea depth measurement with restricted floating sensors
title: Sea Depth Measurement with Restricted Floating Sensors
motivation: Harbor siltation monitoring costs $18M/year, traditional sonar boats are expensive and labor-intensive
problem_framing: Localized sensor nodes float within anchored disk areas; need to estimate floating areas not instantaneous positions
key_insight: Locate constrained mobility areas (disk centered at anchor) rather than tracking mobile sensors, then derive sea depth from rope geometry
method_signature: FALA algorithm: RMED for seeds, regression analysis for non-seeds, triangulate anchor positions
evaluation_criteria: Sea depth estimation error, anchor position error, radius error (<20% relative error target)
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: RSSI-based ranging error up to 150% severely limits FALA accuracy; floating model assumes randomness but near-shore currents are regular
evidence_for_taste: not suitable for resource-restricted sensor nodes
more precise distance estimating techniques would help
we believe a good model of the behaviors of the sea would help diminish their negative impact
thinking_moves: 从定位瞬时位置退化为定位约束区域,降低问题难度
将计算几何最小包围圆问题adapt为在线更新算法
通过样本统计量的线性回归反向推导几何参数
承认物理模型与实际环境的偏差并指出未来改进方向
